checks.invariant: The SessionStart gh probe must not resolve and execute a binary supplied by the opened (possibly third-party) project directory.
checks.result: hooks/stilo-setup.js:8 calls spawnSync('gh.exe'|'gh',['--version'],{timeout:1000,shell:false,windowsHide:true,encoding:'utf8'}) with a bare name and no cwd option, so the child inherits the hook process cwd; hooks/stilo-activate.js:9-10 runs it on every SessionStart from process.cwd(). The only control is shell:false, which prevents shell parsing but does not constrain executable search. No absolute path, no PATH filtering and no explicit safe cwd. Whether the Windows runtime (Node 24 / libuv search_path) checks the current directory before PATH, and whether the host sets cwd to the opened project, are runtime facts not observable without execution; recorded as needs_validation.

checks.invariant: The hook launcher itself must not resolve node from the project directory.
checks.result: hooks/claude-codex-hooks.json:9-10 uses 'node' resolved via PATH (POSIX sh) and PowerShell 'Get-Command node' (PowerShell does not run commands from the current directory without an explicit .\ prefix). The SessionStart matcher (line 5) covers startup|resume|clear|compact, so the probe runs repeatedly. No separate cwd-resolution issue in the launcher from source.

checks.invariant: Lock/receipt reads in the probe must not let project content influence the decision.
checks.result: hooks/stilo-setup.js:11-13 reads only stateDir (STILO_HOME or ~/.stilo/setup, same principal as user); the receipt status interpolated at line 13 is whitelisted by readReceipt. No project-controlled input reaches this branch.

checks.invariant: The lock and receipt writes must not follow a lower-trust actor's symlink or replacement at the leaf, and must create the lock exclusively.
checks.result: Lock is created with writeFileSync(...,{flag:'wx'}) (line 67, O_CREAT|O_EXCL, which fails on an existing leaf including a symlink); the receipt is written to a random-UUID temp name with flag 'wx' (lines 105-106) then renameSync over github-cli.json (line 107), which replaces the directory entry and does not write through a symlink target. The receipt is re-read after taking the lock (lines 70-72). Lock release (line 112) checks the token before unlink; the read/unlink window is reachable only by processes able to write the user's state dir.

checks.invariant: The state directory must be owned by the invoking user, not by a lower-trust principal.
checks.result: defaultStateDir (line 8) is $STILO_HOME/setup or os.homedir()/.stilo/setup. STILO_HOME is set by the user (same principal); the default sits in the user's home, which other OS users cannot normally write. A project directory cannot select stateDir: neither the hook nor the script derives it from cwd or from repo files. No cross-principal ownership boundary is crossed.

checks.invariant: Receipt content must be validated before it drives decisions or text injected into the agent.
checks.result: readReceipt (lines 35-42) requires versionSchema===1, a status in [available, installed, pending, failed] and a string reason. Otherwise it returns {invalid:true}, and any non-ENOENT read error also maps to invalid. The hook injects only the whitelisted status (hooks/stilo-setup.js:13). The script echoes receipt.reason to stdout (line 63), but the file is written by the user's own account.

checks.invariant: Project state discovery must not feed the setup lock/receipt path.
checks.result: hooks/stilo-state.js (findStateFiles/resolveProjeto) handles only .stilo/state.json and checkpoint discovery, and none of its output reaches defaultStateDir or the lock/receipt paths. Its writers are not wired to hooks (per architecture section 4.6) and do not touch ~/.stilo/setup.

checks.invariant: Package-manager and gh spawns made by the agent-run installer must resolve to trusted system binaries, not to files in the working directory where the agent runs the script.
checks.result: realRun (line 16) calls spawn(file,args,{shell:false,windowsHide:true,stdio:[...],env:{...process.env,...}}) with no cwd option, so it inherits the agent's cwd, which is normally the project. Bare names reach it: 'gh.exe'/'gh' (lines 51-52, 96), 'winget.exe' (lines 76, 90-91), 'brew', 'apt-get', 'apt-cache', 'dnf', 'id' (lines 77-87). Only the Windows fallback knownWindowsExecutable (lines 43-44, 56-58, 98-100) is absolute. On Windows, if the runtime searches cwd before PATH, a project-planted winget.exe would run when gh is absent, which is exactly the state in which hooks/stilo-setup.js:17-25 tells the agent to run this script. Decisive runtime fact not observable without execution; recorded as needs_validation.

checks.invariant: No attacker-influenced data may reach spawn arguments or a shell (injection).
checks.result: Every args array is a constant literal (lines 52, 76-77, 79-85, 87, 90-91, 96). shell:false throughout. Explicit .exe names avoid the .bat/.cmd shell-wrapping path. main (lines 116-118) accepts only an optional --retry flag. The inherited env belongs to the user. No injection sink found.

checks.invariant: The Linux and macOS paths must not escalate privilege automatically or resolve from cwd by default.
checks.result: Linux installs only when id -u returns 0 (lines 87-88) and never calls sudo. POSIX spawn uses PATH lookup (execvp semantics), which reaches cwd only if the user's PATH contains '.' or an empty entry, which is user configuration. No default cross-principal path on POSIX.

candidates.title: SessionStart gh probe may run a gh.exe planted in the opened project directory (Windows)
candidates.description: On every SessionStart (startup, resume, clear, compact), the hook calls spawnSync('gh.exe', ['--version'], {shell:false}). It passes a bare name and sets no cwd, so the child inherits the project directory as its cwd. If the Windows process-spawn path in Node/libuv searches the current directory before PATH, a cloned third-party repository containing gh.exe at the opened directory runs that binary as the user. This happens automatically on session start, with no agent tool call and no host tool-permission prompt.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: probeGitHubCli resolves the executable by bare name. It relies on shell:false as its only control and sets no explicit trusted cwd, no absolute path and no PATH filtering. Executable search order is left to the platform's runtime, while the cwd is the lower-trust project directory.

trace.description: Host runs node stilo-activate.js on startup|resume|clear|compact (matcher at line 5), with the session's working directory.
Calls probeGitHubCli() unconditionally, with the process cwd being the opened project.
spawnSync('gh.exe',['--version'],{timeout:1000,shell:false,windowsHide:true}): bare name, no cwd option, inherited env; process creation is the sink.

evidence.description: Bare-name gh.exe spawn without cwd or absolute path; shell:false is the only control.
Hook operates on process.cwd(), which is the project directory (docs/contrato-hooks.md:41 states the hook runs with the session cwd).
Matcher startup|resume|clear|compact makes the probe run at every session start and context reset.

blockers: Not observable without execution (no OS sandbox on this host): whether Node 24.19.0 / libuv uv_spawn on Windows, with shell:false and a bare file name such as 'gh.exe', searches the child's cwd before PATH, and whether it honors NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath.

Host fact: whether Claude Code and Codex start SessionStart plugin hooks with the opened project directory as process cwd, and whether a workspace-trust prompt precedes plugin hooks. If trust already permits repo-defined hooks (for example .claude/settings.json), the boundary crossed is smaller, though the planted file is stealthier and plugin-scoped.

validation_plan.local: In a disposable Windows VM with Node 24.19.0 and gh not installed or on PATH, create an empty directory containing a copy of a benign system binary renamed gh.exe (for example hostname.exe). From that directory, run a minimal harness: node -e "const r=require('child_process').spawnSync('gh.exe',['--version'],{shell:false,encoding:'utf8'});console.log(r.error&&r.error.code,r.stdout)". If stdout shows the hostname instead of ENOENT, the cwd copy was executed. Repeat with NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1 set.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner observes in Claude Code and in Codex on Windows, opening a dummy project folder, which process cwd the SessionStart hook receives (for example by temporarily logging process.cwd() from a local copy of the plugin) and whether a folder-trust prompt is shown before plugin hooks run.

candidates.title: Agent-run GitHub CLI installer may run a project-planted winget.exe or gh.exe (Windows)
candidates.description: When the probe reports gh absent, the SessionStart note tells the agent to run node <pluginRoot>/scripts/setup-github-cli.js. The script's realRun spawns bare names ('gh.exe', then 'winget.exe') with shell:false, inherited env and no cwd, so they run in the agent's working directory, normally the project. A repository that plants winget.exe (but not gh.exe, which keeps the probe at 'absent' and makes the setup note appear) would have its binary launched as the user if Windows executable search includes the current directory first. The host tool-permission prompt shows only 'node .../setup-github-cli.js', not the binary that is actually resolved.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: realRun resolves installer and probe executables by bare name and inherits the caller's cwd. There is no absolute path resolution (for example a PATH lookup that excludes cwd, or a fixed System32/WindowsApps path for winget) and no explicit trusted cwd. Only the knownWindowsExecutable fallback is absolute.

trace.description: The SessionStart context tells the agent to execute node with the setup-github-cli.js path when the probe status is 'absent'.
First invoke('gh.exe',['--version']). On ENOENT, the script continues to the install path.
spawn(file,args,{shell:false,windowsHide:true,stdio:[...],env:{...process.env,...}}) with no cwd option: process creation resolved from the inherited cwd and PATH.

evidence.description: spawn without cwd option and with a bare file name passed by callers.
Only knownWindowsExecutable uses an absolute path, which shows the sibling control is not applied to winget.exe or gh.exe.
The setup note is emitted only when the probe status is 'absent' (gh ENOENT, no lock or receipt), which is the precondition an attacker gets by planting winget.exe without gh.exe.

blockers: Not observable without execution (no OS sandbox on this host): whether Node 24.19.0 / libuv on Windows searches the current directory before PATH for bare names such as 'winget.exe' with shell:false.

Host or agent fact: which cwd the AI agent uses when it runs the setup script (the project directory is expected but depends on the agent's Bash or PowerShell tool), and whether the host permission prompt is shown and approved for that command.

validation_plan.local: In a disposable Windows VM with Node 24.19.0, no gh, and a benign binary renamed winget.exe (for example hostname.exe) in an otherwise empty directory, run from that directory: node -e "require('child_process').spawn('winget.exe',['--version'],{shell:false,stdio:['ignore','pipe','pipe']}).stdout.on('data',d=>console.log(String(d)))". Output from the renamed binary instead of the system winget confirms cwd-first resolution. Do not run the real installer.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner observes, in a dummy project in Claude Code and in Codex on Windows, the working directory the agent uses when it follows the setup note (for example by running a local copy of the script that prints process.cwd() and exits).

hardening: hooks/stilo-setup.js:8 and scripts/setup-github-cli.js:16: pass an explicit trusted cwd (for example os.homedir() or the plugin root) and resolve executables to absolute paths by walking PATH while skipping '.', empty and relative entries. On Windows, prefer known locations (%ProgramFiles%\GitHub CLI\gh.exe, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps\winget.exe). Add a regression test that plants a dummy gh.exe or winget.exe in the cwd and asserts the resolved path is outside it.

scripts/setup-github-cli.js:112: lock release reads then unlinks by path (non-atomic). This is acceptable because only the user's own processes can write the state dir, but it could be tightened with an fd-based compare if STILO_HOME is ever allowed to point to a shared directory.

scripts/setup-github-cli.js:66: mkdirSync(stateDir,{recursive:true}) uses the default mode. If STILO_HOME points to a shared location such as /tmp, another user could pre-create the directory. Consider mode 0o700 and an ownership check (fs.statSync(dir).uid===process.getuid()) on POSIX.
